acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Wolves family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Gray Wolf, T1, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Flank-Probe Initiate archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Lean ordinary wolf with a gray coat, long legs, intact ears, light rib visibility, and no equipment.
Signature mechanic: Cross-Step Trip: the Gray Wolf crosses its outside forepaw inward before lunging at the target's rear leg.
battlefieldDuty: Circle toward an exposed side and commit to one tripping bite when the target turns away.
constructionDimensions: Mineral accretion stays localized to load-bearing shoulders, paws, brow, and scar ridges while most fur and hide remain visible.
Weighted steps compress dust and lift detached stones around the animal rather than replacing its body with rock.
counterplay: Face the Wolf or step across its approach, then punish the missed bite during the low recovery. Affinity signal: A pale fracture line opens across the loaded paw or shoulder after a planted lunge or command stance.
forbiddenTreatments: Pasted rocks that conceal joints or fur direction
identityInvariants: Every form retains a four-legged lupine skeleton, long muzzle, visible paws, expressive ears, and a readable tail; no form becomes humanoid or wears manufactured armor.
Rank is communicated through chest mass, coat mantle, scars, posture, and pack behavior rather than arbitrary glow or simple scale.
Pack attack direction remains readable through gaze, ear position, tail line, paw placement, and the spacing of companion Wolves.
telegraph: Its shoulders drop and the outside forepaw crosses inward while its gaze fixes on the exposed leg.
